transformations.formula: Normalize WMO global glacier mass loss while retaining the separate assessment that most smaller-glacier regions likely passed peak water.
Normalize the lower-bound population relying on glacier and snow melt; do not relabel it as observed shortage.
Use the source-reported consecutive years in which all assessed glaciated regions lost mass.
Divide glaciated regions with loss by all assessed glaciated regions.

receipts.uncertainty: The WMO global mass estimate combines about 500 field-monitored glaciers and geodetic measurements covering more than 200,000 glaciers. Preliminary 2024 observations, regional scaling and mass-balance methods affect the estimate. The human figure covers melt from glaciers and snow and must not be interpreted as glacier-only volume share or observed shortage.
receipts.freshness: Reviewed global assessment snapshot; latest quantitative observation period ends 2024.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: WMO and UNESCO quantify global glacier loss, all-region persistence, meltwater-dependent population and the current assessment that most smaller-glacier regions likely passed peak water.
higher_priority_failures: No basin-complete annual global runoff series supports a current-data score.
